Summary Collaboration Themes: This collaboration bridges the gap between systems-level behavioral neuroscience and molecular synaptic physiology. By integrating Justin S. Rhodes' expertise in exercise physiology, nutritional genomics, and behavioral phenotyping with Nien-Pei Tsai's specialization in ubiquitin-mediated synaptic homeostasis, ER stress, and epilepsy mechanisms, the partnership aims to uncover the precise molecular pathways through which lifestyle factors (exercise, diet) modulate brain plasticity, seizure susceptibility, and cognitive health. Key themes include the genetic and molecular basis of exercise-induced neuroprotection, the role of protein degradation in synaptic plasticity, and the development of multi-modal strategies for treating neurological disorders.
